about.description: OnRe provides tokenized access to private credit and structured finance products, connecting institutional lenders with decentralized liquidity. It enables securitization of off-chain credit through on-chain smart contracts.
about.registryInfo: On Re SAC Ltd. - exempted limited company registered in Bermuda as a Segregated Accounts Company (SAC) under the Segregated Accounts Companies Act 2000, company number 55347, licensed and regulated by the Bermuda Monetary Authority with a Class F licence under the Digital Asset Business Act 2018 and a Class IIGB insurance licence under the Insurance Act 1978.
about.founders: Dan Roberts (Co-Founder, CEO), Theodore Georgas (Co-Founder, CTO)
about.regulatoryStatus: On Re SAC Ltd. is authorised and regulated by the Bermuda Monetary Authority under a Class IIGB Innovative Insurer General Business licence and a Class F full licence under the Digital Asset Business Act 2018, registration 55347 effective May 2022. The company states it was the first reinsurer approved under both regimes after graduating from the BMA regulatory sandbox. Founded as Nayms in 2019 and rebranded to OnRe in May 2025.
about.keyMilestones: 2026-05: 5 million Series A co led by Forward Industries and RockawayX | 2026-02: reached 100 million AUM | 2025-10: ONyc Global Access permissionless channel launched | 2025-08: ONyc listed on Kamino as first reinsurance backed collateral in Solana DeFi | 2025-05: Nayms rebranded to OnRe with the ONe product launch
about.entityStructureNotes: On Re SAC Ltd. is a Bermuda Segregated Accounts Company that both underwrites reinsurance and issues the tokens. ONyc represents a proportional claim on a ring fenced segregated account that is statutorily separate from the general account under the Segregated Accounts Companies Act 2000.

fees.revenueNotes: Minting costs network fees only and fulfilled redemptions carry a 25 bps fee subject to change. Collateral returns on backing assets are an explicit ONyc yield component with any retained spread undisclosed.
